decisive_items: 24-hour urinary metanephrines >10 000 µg (normal 25–312 µg) and normetanephrines 8791 µg (normal <600 µg)
response.rationale: The co-occurrence of markedly elevated metanephrines indicating pheochromocytoma and markedly elevated calcitonin/CEA with thyroid nodules indicating medullary thyroid carcinoma is the classic MEN2A combination. Absent family history does not exclude de novo presentation.

rejected.why: This is a broad MEN2 label, while the supplied findings of MTC plus pheochromocytoma support the more specific MEN2A subtype.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma alone explains calcitonin, CEA, and thyroid nodules, but not the massive pheochromocytoma-range metanephrine elevation.
Pheochromocytoma alone explains episodic symptoms and metanephrines, but not the profoundly elevated calcitonin, CEA, and calcified thyroid/submental lesions.
